name: United States
tagline: Four years, no fixed major on day one, and a very wide price range
summary: An American bachelor's degree takes four years and starts broad: you take courses across several fields and usually declare a major at the end of year two. Admission is 'holistic' - your grades matter most, but so do essays, teacher references, what you do outside school, and increasingly again the SAT or ACT. As a European student you are an international applicant everywhere, so you pay the published sticker price unless a university gives you financial aid, and only a handful of universities give internationals enough aid to make it affordable. The cost range is enormous: for 2026-27 a full year runs from about 62,000 USD (about €54,500) for an international student at Illinois to 95,000-100,000 USD (about €83,600–88,000, at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) at Harvard before health insurance.
whyConsider: You do not have to choose your subject before you arrive - you can start in autumn 2027 and declare a major in 2029.
A small group of very wealthy private universities and liberal arts colleges will meet 100% of your assessed financial need, including flights, no matter what your family earns.
Good HL results often convert into real course credit, which can let you skip introductory courses or even finish early.
Liberal arts colleges are small (1,500-2,500 students), taught by professors rather than teaching assistants, and several (Amherst, Bowdoin) are need-blind for internationals.
Research, internships and campus jobs are built into the undergraduate experience.
You do not have to choose your subject before you arrive — you can start in autumn 2027 and declare a major in 2029.

A small group of very wealthy private universities and liberal arts colleges meet 100% of assessed financial need for international students. Harvard states plainly that international students are eligible for exactly the same aid as Americans and that families earning under 100,000 USD pay nothing.

Higher Level results can convert into real course credit. The University of California publishes a rate card — 8 quarter units per HL exam at 5, 6 or 7, plus 6 for the diploma itself at 30 points or more — which is worth about a term of a four-year degree.

Liberal arts colleges are small, taught by professors rather than teaching assistants, and several (Amherst, Bowdoin) are need-blind for international students. Several charge no application fee at all.
The community-college transfer route — two years at an Associate degree, then two years at a university — is a much cheaper way into an American bachelor's degree, and few IB students hear about it.
watchOuts: Sticker price. Harvard's published billed cost for 2026-27 is 91,634 USD for one year, and that is before health insurance and flights.
Most universities are need-aware for internationals: asking for money reduces your chance of getting in. Only a very short list is need-blind for non-Americans.
The testing landscape flipped back. Harvard and Yale both require the SAT or ACT again for autumn 2027 entry, and IB results do not substitute for the test at Yale.

Deadlines are brutally early: early rounds close between 1 and 15 November 2026, Regular Decision between 1 and 15 January 2027, and the University of California closes 30 November 2026 - all long before you sit your IB exams.
Immigration costs and admin are real: I-20, SEVIS fee, embassy interview, and post-study work depends on an OPT approval you cannot count on.

There is no American deadline. Among the fourteen institutions covered here the regular round closes on 30 November, 1 January, 2 January, 4 January, 5 January and 15 January, and the early round runs from 1 to 15 November. Carrying one institution's date to another is an expensive mistake, because nothing reopens afterwards — there is no Clearing, no late round and no second intake.

An IB Diploma removes nothing by itself. Yale requires the SAT or ACT from every applicant and states that IB results may accompany the score but not replace it; MIT requires it too. Harvard accepts IB actual or predicted scores only where testing is genuinely inaccessible, which Copenhagen is not. If a selective university is on your list, book a test date in 2026.

Early Decision is a contract, not a preference. Amherst's wording is that you agree not to be an Early Decision candidate anywhere else and, if admitted, to withdraw your applications from other colleges and enrol. It raises your odds and it ends your ability to compare financial aid offers, which for a family paying from outside the US is usually the more expensive loss.

Financial aid is applied for with the application, not after it. Grinnell requires every aid form by the application deadline; Macalester states that aid cannot be awarded after an offer of admission has been made, and not at any later point in the degree either.

What an IB Diploma is worth in credit varies from a full term to nothing, at institutions that are equally official about it. An HL Physics 6 is 8 quarter units at Berkeley and zero at MIT, which gives credit only at grade 7 and none at all for IB Biology or Chemistry. Read the credit page of every institution on your list before you apply.

Health insurance is compulsory, expensive and charged automatically. Every registered Berkeley student including international students is enrolled in the campus plan unless they waive it; in Massachusetts it is state law. A policy bought in Denmark or elsewhere in Europe may be comprehensive and still fail the waiver because it is not accessible where you are living.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national minimum. Selective universities look at the whole transcript and at HL subject choice rather than at a points threshold. Higher Level subjects are what earn credit; Standard Level rarely does.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: There is no national IB-to-GPA conversion. Each university reads your IB predicted grades and, later, your final July results directly. The University of California publishes a credit conversion: a full IB Diploma with 30+ points earns 6 quarter units, and each Higher Level exam graded 5, 6 or 7 earns 8 quarter units (5.3 semester units), usually 24 quarter units in total.
notes: Credit for HL 5+ is common but the rules differ at every single university - check the specific university's IB credit page, not a general guide.
Yale states that IB results may be added to an application but cannot replace the required SAT or ACT score.
Harvard will accept IB scores instead of the SAT/ACT only where testing is genuinely unavailable, not as a normal alternative.
Your school sends predicted grades; final results arrive 6 July 2027, well after decisions. Offers are effectively made on predictions plus everything else in the file.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Everything. The question is not whether the degree is in English but whether you must prove your English.
language.englishProof: Many universities waive TOEFL/IELTS for students who have been taught in English, which an IB Diploma from an English-medium programme normally demonstrates - but the waiver is not automatic and each university sets its own rule. Check the specific university; where no waiver applies, typical requirements are TOEFL iBT 100+ or IELTS 7.0+ at selective universities. Check each university's own threshold.
notes: Your IB English A Literature or Language and Literature result is the strongest evidence you can offer, but ask each admissions office in writing whether it replaces the test.
Some universities also use the Duolingo English Test. Availability varies year to year.

feeContext.summary: At a public university an international student pays the non-resident rate for all four years, because residency for tuition is not something an F-1 student acquires by living in the state. The University of California publishes both figures for 2027–28: UC Tuition of 16,278 USD for a California resident and 57,300 USD for a nonresident, with a total on-campus cost of attendance of 49,078 and 90,100 USD. UC also holds its tuition line flat for up to six years under a Tuition Stability Plan. The other public universities here publish 2026–27 figures: Michigan charges non-residents 67,096 USD in tuition and fees in the first two years of LSA (total budget 88,394 USD), Illinois quotes 42,248–53,078 USD for international students (total 62,146–72,976 USD), and Arizona State puts an international student's total at 69,906 USD (about €61,500 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026).

feeContext.summary: At a private university or liberal arts college there is one published price for everyone and the real question is how much of it is discounted. Harvard's 2026–27 billed cost is 91,634 USD, with health insurance a further 4,954 USD — and Harvard also states that international students are eligible for exactly the same aid as Americans, that it meets 100% of demonstrated need and that families earning under 100,000 USD contribute nothing. Between those two extremes sit institutions like Grinnell, which considers your need when deciding whom to admit and then meets 100% of it for those it takes. The aid application is due with the admission application, and Macalester states that aid cannot be awarded after an offer has been made.

Harvard states that international students are eligible for exactly the same financial aid as American students, that it meets 100 percent of demonstrated need, that families earning under 100,000 USD are expected to contribute nothing, and that it never requires a student to borrow.

Grinnell takes international applicants through the Common Application with Early Decision I closing 15 November, Early Decision II 5 January and Regular Decision 15 January, requires all financial aid forms by the same deadline as the application, considers demonstrated need when deciding whom to admit, and then meets 100 percent of institutionally determined need for those it admits.

Macalester takes international first-year applicants through the Common App with Early Decision I and Early Action closing 1 November, Early Decision II 1 January and Regular Decision 15 January, and states that financial aid cannot be awarded after an offer of admission has been made, so aid must be requested during the application.

livingContext.healthcare: Compulsory, expensive, and charged to the bill automatically rather than offered. Every registered UC Berkeley student, international students included, is enrolled in the campus plan at 2,533 USD (about €2,230 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) per semester for undergraduates in 2026–27 unless they waive it with proof of comparable cover. In Massachusetts it is state law: Harvard states that Massachusetts law requires any full-time or part-time student at an institution of higher learning in the state to hold qualifying student health insurance or comparable cover, and its waiver closes on 31 July. A Danish travel or study policy may be comprehensive and still fail, because a waiver also requires the cover to be reasonably accessible where you are living.
livingContext.residency: There is no free movement of any kind. After you accept an offer the institution issues Form I-20, you pay the 350 USD I-901 SEVIS fee, complete the DS-160 and attend an F-1 visa interview at the US Embassy in Copenhagen, bringing the SEVIS receipt with you.

sectorLandscape.summary: American higher education has no ministry and no national structure, so the sectors are not legal categories — they are recognisable kinds of institution with different sizes, prices, admission behaviour and purposes, and the names below are the ones Americans actually use. A full IB Diploma opens all of them. Two are easy to miss, at opposite ends: the liberal arts college, which is small, teaching-led and often generous to international students, and the community college, a much cheaper way into an American bachelor's degree that English-language advice rarely mentions.

routes.what: Endowed, independent of any state government, and running graduate schools alongside the undergraduate college — Harvard, Yale, Stanford, NYU. One published price for everyone, which is very high, discounted by need-based aid that at a handful of them is extraordinarily generous to international applicants and at most of them is not offered to them at all. Admission is holistic, opaque and at some of them in the low single digits for international applicants.
routes.note: The sector English-language advice is almost always describing when it says "applying to America", and the sector a realistic list cannot be built entirely out of.

routes.what: Small — often 1,500 to 2,500 students — almost always residential, undergraduate only, with no graduate students competing for a professor's attention and classes taught by professors rather than teaching assistants. Amherst runs an open curriculum with no distribution requirements at all. The breadth-then-depth shape is close to the IB Diploma, and several of these colleges are more generous to international students, and cheaper to apply to, than the research universities: Colby charges no application fee.
routes.note: Often mistaken for a lesser option by students who have never heard of the names. Many are highly selective, and they suit a student who wants to be taught rather than lectured.

routes.what: Owned by a state and built to educate its residents — Michigan, Illinois, Berkeley, Arizona State. Large, strong in engineering and the sciences, and priced in two tiers: a resident rate and a non-resident rate that an international student pays for all four years. Institutional aid for international students is limited or absent; Michigan states that international students on temporary visas should expect to pay the full cost of attendance. These are also the institutions where the application route is least predictable, because some are on the Common App and some are on their own state system.
routes.note: The sector where the difference between 16,278 and 57,300 USD a year is decided by something a foreign student cannot acquire.

routes.what: Two-year institutions awarding an Associate of Arts or Associate of Science, with open or flexible admission, small classes and fees a fraction of a university's. The point for a foreign student is the "2+2": two years at a community college followed by two years at a university, leaving with the university's bachelor's degree. Six University of California campuses — Davis, Irvine, Merced, Riverside, Santa Barbara and Santa Cruz — operate a Transfer Admission Guarantee that turns the second half into a published promise rather than a hope.
routes.note: A cheap route into an American degree, and a rarely mentioned one. One gap: whether an F-1 student from Denmark can hold a Transfer Admission Guarantee on the same terms as a Californian resident is not established here, and nobody should plan around it until it is.

routes.what: Science and engineering institutions with a common technical core — MIT is the archetype. Everyone takes the same mathematics and physics in the first year, the pace assumes strong Higher Level mathematics, and the admission process is often run outside the shared application systems entirely.
routes.note: Also a sector where an IB student may get nothing for Higher Level results. MIT grants credit only at grade 7 and none at all in Biology or Chemistry.

routes.what: Independent schools of art, design, music, dance and theatre, admitting on portfolio or audition. Grades matter less, the portfolio matters more than anything else, and the calendar and the supplementary steps are different from everything else on this page — Stanford's arts-supplement deadline, for example, falls two to four weeks ahead of the ordinary one.
routes.note: Not covered in detail on this site; a student who needs it will not find it in the ordinary listings.

routes.what: Degree-granting institutions run as businesses, marketed heavily to international students and to adult learners, with admission requirements that are often nominal.
routes.note: A student searching online will often meet it first. Its accreditation, transferability, visa status and value are not covered here, so check each before considering one.

sources.title: Community colleges offer two-year Associate of Arts or Associate of Science programmes, are usually less expensive than four-year institutions, and support a "2+2" route in which two years of community college are followed by two years of university study toward a bachelor's degree.

Six University of California campuses — Davis, Irvine, Merced, Riverside, Santa Barbara and Santa Cruz — offer a Transfer Admission Guarantee, submitted in the 1–30 September window for a fall start, with each campus's own requirements set out in a separate TAG matrix.

For 2027–28 the University of California publishes UC Tuition of 16,278 USD for California residents and 57,300 USD for nonresidents, with a total on-campus cost of attendance of 49,078 USD and 90,100 USD respectively, and states that UC Tuition remains flat for up to six years under the Tuition Stability Plan.

MIT gives credit only for Higher Level IB exams, only at grade 7, gives no credit at all for IB Biology, Chemistry or Information Technology in a Global Society, and gives 18.01 for HL Mathematics, 8.01 for HL Physics and nine units of unrestricted elective credit for each applicable humanities, arts or social science exam.
Colby College is a live Common Application member for first-year applicants, charges no application fee, is test optional or test flexible, and offers aid to international students.

jurisdictions.name: The Common App colleges
jurisdictions.summary: Twelve of the fourteen institutions here, spread across all ten states covered here, on one form. A private research university in Massachusetts and a public flagship in Illinois are on exactly the same application with exactly the same submission items; what differs between them is the round they offer, the date they close and whether they require a test.

Everyone replies on 1 May 2027.

jurisdictions.name: The University of California
jurisdictions.summary: A genuine sub-national admissions authority: nine campuses, one application, one filing window, one set of rules set by the Regents rather than by the campus. Berkeley is the campus on this page and adding the other eight costs only the fee. Everything a student learns about applying to the Common App colleges has to be unlearned here.

variations.label: One window, 1 October to 30 November
variations.summary: The fall 2027 application opens for drafting on 1 August 2026, is filed between 1 October and 30 November 2026, and is not accepted a day either side. There is no Early Decision, no Early Action, no rolling consideration and no late round. Decisions arrive across March 2027, the Statement of Intent to Register is due on 1 May 2027, and official IB results must reach the campus by 15 July 2027 — nine days after the IB publishes them.

sources.title: For fall 2027 entry the University of California application opens on 1 August 2026, must be filed between 1 October and 30 November 2026, decisions are released during March 2027, admitted first-year students must submit their Statement of Intent to Register by 1 May 2027, and official IB examination results must reach the campus by 15 July 2027.

deadlines.label: Applications close — and there is no American closing date, because no American body sets one
deadlines.notes: A single American deadline does not exist. There is no ministry, no clearing house and no national closing day; every college sets its own, and four different rounds run on four different promises. The shape, from the colleges on this page: Early Action, Restrictive Early Action and Single-Choice Early Action all close 1 November 2026 (Harvard, Stanford, Yale, Illinois, Macalester) and are not binding. Early Decision II closes in early January 2027 — Macalester 1 January, Colby 4 January, Bowdoin and Grinnell 5 January — and is also binding. Regular Decision closes between 1 and 15 January 2027 — Harvard 1 January, Yale 2 January, MIT and Colby 4 January, Stanford, Amherst and Illinois 5 January, Grinnell and Macalester 15 January. The University of California closes on 30 November 2026 and has its own entry below. After a college's own Regular Decision date that college is finished for the year: there is no Clearing, no late round and no second intake. Write each college's own date into your own calendar and do not carry one college's date to another.

deadlines.label: Early Decision is binding — applying early is a commitment, not an early submission

deadlines.notes: What you need to know about Early Decision is not when it closes but what signing it costs you. Early Decision I (1 to 15 November 2026) and Early Decision II (early January 2027) are binding in the strongest sense the American system has. Amherst's wording is that you agree not to be an Early Decision candidate anywhere else and, if admitted, to withdraw your applications from every other college and enrol. It is a signed agreement — student, parent and school counsellor — filed inside the Common App for one college only. Two consequences follow and neither is obvious from a calendar. First, an admitted Early Decision applicant does not get the 1 May reply date: that decision was made in November. Second, and for a family paying from abroad this is usually the more expensive loss, you can never compare financial aid offers, because you will only ever hold one. Early Action, Restrictive Early Action and Single-Choice Early Action are NOT binding — you keep every offer and still reply on 1 May — but Stanford's and Yale's restrict where else you may apply early, so they still decide your whole autumn in October. Missing an early round costs you that round's higher admit rate; signing an Early Decision agreement costs you the choice.

steps: From spring 2026, build a list of 8-12 institutions in three groups: places that meet full need for internationals, places likely to give you merit money, and one or two you could genuinely afford at full price.

Work out which of the three application environments each one sits in. Twelve of the fourteen here are on the Common App; Berkeley is on the University of California application and closes a month earlier; MIT takes only its own.
Register for and sit the SAT or ACT in 2026 if any institution on your list requires it, and plan a retake date before November. Yale and MIT require it and do not accept the IB instead.
Create a Common App account when it opens on 31 July 2026, fill in your personal details once, and add your institutions.

Ask two teachers and your studievejleder for references in spring 2026, not in October. Your counsellor also uploads the school report and your predicted IB grades - Illinois wants those a week after the application itself.
Write the 650-word personal essay over the summer, then the supplemental essays. The University of California asks four 350-word personal insight questions instead and needs writing of its own.
File the University of California application between 1 October and 30 November 2026. It closes before every Regular Decision deadline, and there is no second round.

Submit early-round applications - 1 November for Early Action almost everywhere, between 1 and 15 November for Early Decision depending on the college - then the Regular Decision applications between 1 and 15 January 2027.
Submit financial aid forms by the same deadline as the application, not later. Macalester states that aid cannot be awarded after an offer of admission is made.
Decide by 1 May 2027, then wait for the I-20, pay the 350 USD SEVIS fee and book an embassy appointment in Copenhagen for the F-1 visa.
Arrange the compulsory student health insurance, or a waiver, before the July deadline. In Massachusetts it is required by state law.
application.selectionNotes: Holistic review at most institutions: no published points threshold, no ranking table, no guaranteed entry. Committees read grades and the rigour of your subjects first, then essays, references, activities and context, and at many institutions also your ability to pay. Early Decision is binding - Amherst's wording is that you agree to withdraw your applications from other colleges and enrol - and it meaningfully raises your odds, but it removes your ability to compare financial aid offers. Early Action and Restrictive Early Action are not binding, though Stanford's and Yale's restrict where else you may apply early. The University of California does not run any early round at all, does not read letters of recommendation, and asks four short personal insight questions instead of an essay. Arizona State does not run a tournament at all: it admits against published criteria on a rolling basis. International admit rates at the most selective universities are in the low single digits; do not build a list out of them.

tuitionEuEea.value: Not applicable - the United States does not have an EU/EEA fee category. As an international applicant you pay the international or out-of-state rate everywhere.

tuitionNonEu.value: Private universities: Harvard's published billed cost for 2026-27 is 91,634 USD (tuition 62,226, fees 6,216, housing 14,250, food 8,942), with total billed and unbilled costs of 95,134-100,134 USD plus 4,954 USD health insurance if you are not covered elsewhere. Public universities: UC Berkeley's 2026-27 tuition and fees for a new student are 18,214 USD, but new out-of-state students pay an additional Nonresident Supplemental Tuition of 39,270 USD, so an international first-year pays roughly 57,500 USD in tuition and fees and a total cost of attendance around 94,000 USD in a residence hall. Michigan's 2026-27 non-resident tuition and fees are 67,096 USD in the first two years of LSA (total budget 88,394 USD); Illinois quotes 42,248-53,078 USD in tuition and fees for international students (total 62,146-72,976 USD); Arizona State's international total for 2026-27 is 69,906 USD.

costs.applicationFee: Harvard 95 USD; Stanford 100 USD; MIT, Amherst and Michigan 75 USD; Arizona State 90 USD for international applicants; University of California 95 USD per campus for international applicants (80 USD for domestic); Grinnell nothing. Fee waivers exist but are usually aimed at low-income US students.

livingCostMonthly.value: Not published as a monthly figure. American universities publish an annual 'cost of attendance' that already includes housing, food, books, transport and personal expenses - see the tuition figures above. UC Berkeley's 2026-27 estimate for housing and utilities in an off-campus apartment is 14,386 USD for a nine-month academic year, about 1,609 USD a month.

notes: Always read the 'cost of attendance', never the tuition line alone. The COA is also the number financial aid is calculated against.
Health insurance is compulsory and charged separately at most universities. Harvard's is 4,954 USD for 2026-27.
Budget for flights home twice a year; Harvard's 2026-27 budget allows 0-5,000 USD for transportation, while Berkeley's standard budget covers only local transport (754-1,238 USD).
The I-901 SEVIS fee is 350 USD for F-1 students, paid before your visa interview.

Not confirmed on an official page: the nonimmigrant visa application (MRV) fee is widely reported as 185 USD, and a new 250 USD Visa Integrity Fee was introduced by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act with effect from 1 October 2025; whether it is being collected yet is not confirmed. Check current fees at travel.state.gov before you budget.

funding: Need-based institutional aid. A short list of universities is need-blind for international applicants and meets 100% of assessed need. Harvard states plainly that international students are eligible for exactly the same aid as Americans, that admission is need-blind, and that families earning under 100,000 USD pay nothing, while families up to 200,000 USD have tuition covered. Yale, MIT, Amherst and Bowdoin state the same need-blind, full-need policy for international students on their own pages. Princeton, Dartmouth, Brown, Notre Dame and Washington and Lee are widely reported to belong to the group but are not confirmed here - confirm on each university's own financial aid page before you apply.

Need-aware full-need aid. Many strong liberal arts colleges consider your finances when deciding but then meet 100% of need if they admit you. Grinnell College is explicit about this: need-aware for internationals, then 100% of institutionally determined need met.

Merit scholarships. Some universities award merit money regardless of need - Grinnell says outstanding international applicants are considered for merit aid whether or not they apply for need-based help. Merit awards are usually partial, 10,000-30,000 USD a year.

Athletic scholarships (NCAA). Real but narrow. Division I and II programmes can offer athletic money; Division III, which includes most liberal arts colleges, cannot offer any athletic aid at all. You must register with the NCAA Eligibility Center and be recruited by a coach - you cannot apply for an athletic scholarship the way you apply for a grant. For an international IB student this is realistic only in sports where you already compete at national level, typically rowing, swimming, football, handball, golf or tennis.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting. The application has its own deadlines.

funding: US federal student loans are not available to international students, and most private US loans require a US co-signer.
workRights: On an F-1 visa you may work on campus during your studies, subject to limits set by your university, and off-campus work generally requires prior authorisation. After your degree, Optional Practical Training (OPT) gives up to 12 months of work authorisation directly related to your major, and graduates of approved STEM degrees can apply for a further 24-month extension if the employer is enrolled in E-Verify. You cannot start OPT until USCIS approves Form I-765 and you receive the Employment Authorization Document. Source: https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/students-and-exchange-visitors/optional-practical-training-opt-for-f-1-students
residency: There is no EU-style free movement. After you accept an offer the university issues Form I-20, you pay the I-901 SEVIS fee of 350 USD, complete the DS-160 form, pay the visa fee and attend an interview at the US Embassy in Copenhagen for an F-1 student visa. Bring the SEVIS receipt to the interview - it is required. You may enter the US up to 30 days before your programme starts. Sources: https://www.ice.gov/sevis/i901 and https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/prepare/paying-the-i-901-sevis-fee
housing: Almost all universities house first-year students on campus and many require it. That is a genuine advantage over Europe: you do not hunt for a room, you get assigned one, and the cost is in the published cost of attendance. Harvard's 2026-27 housing and food come to 23,192 USD; Berkeley's residence hall housing and meal plan for 2026-27 are 16,640 USD and 7,000 USD. From year two, many students move off campus, which is where costs and hassle rise - Berkeley budgets 14,386 USD for nine months in an off-campus apartment.
healthcare: Health insurance is compulsory and expensive, and the Danish yellow card and EHIC are worthless in the US. Universities charge their own student health plan unless you can prove equivalent cover - Harvard's is 4,954 USD and Berkeley's SHIP 5,066 USD for 2026-27 (about €4,360 and €4,460 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026). Private Danish travel or study insurance sometimes qualifies for a waiver, but the university decides and the waiver deadline is usually 1 July. Assume you will pay for the university plan.

systems.name: The Common Application

jurisdiction.area: Member colleges across the United States and abroad

coverage.includes: Most private research universities and liberal arts colleges, and a large and growing number of public universities. Twelve of the fourteen institutions in this profile take it, including four public universities.
coverage.excludes: The University of California, which runs its own application, and institutions that take only their own — MIT is the best-known. Several member colleges also accept the Coalition Application on Scoir or the QuestBridge Application as equal alternatives, so the Common App is the widest front door rather than the only one.

choiceRules.note: There is no limit on the number of colleges and no ranking: you pay a fee at each one and you may hold every offer you receive until the reply date. The one real constraint is self-imposed — an Early Decision agreement is binding, so you may make it with exactly one college, and doing so ends your ability to compare what the others would have offered.

systems.identityRequirement: A Common App account, opened in the applicant's own name. No national digital identity is involved, which makes this one of the few systems in this dataset a non-resident can enter without a local ID.
sharedSteps: Open the account and complete the common section once: personal details, family, education, activities, and the 650-word personal essay.
Add each college, then complete that college's own supplement — usually further essays, and Harvard alone asks five short answers.
Invite the school counsellor and teachers as recommenders. The school report and predicted IB grades are uploaded by the school, not by the student.
Choose a round at each college separately. The same application can be Early Decision at one, Early Action at another and Regular Decision at a third.
Pay a fee at each college, or request a waiver. Fees in this profile run from nothing at Colby to 100 USD at Stanford.
systems.decisionModel: Each college decides on its own, in its own committee, on its own calendar. The Common App transmits the application and nothing else — it does not rank, match, allocate or hold a place. Two colleges reading the same file may reach opposite conclusions, and neither has to explain why.
systems.replyModel: Offers are held open to the national candidates' reply date of 1 May, so a student normally chooses between offers with the financial aid figures in front of them. The exception is Early Decision, where accepting is agreed in advance and every other application is withdrawn.

sources.title: The Common Application opened its 2026-27 season — the cycle for entry in autumn 2027 — on 31 July 2026.

Harvard requires the Common Application from every first-year applicant, international and American alike, with a Restrictive Early Action deadline of 1 November and a Regular Decision deadline of 1 January, a 95 USD fee, a required SAT or ACT, and IB actual or predicted scores accepted in place of a test only where testing is genuinely inaccessible.

Yale accepts the Common Application, the Coalition Application on SCOIR and the QuestBridge Application, with a Single-Choice Early Action deadline of 1 November and a Regular Decision deadline of 2 January.

notes: The Coalition Application on Scoir and the QuestBridge Application are named by Yale, Amherst and Bowdoin as equal alternatives to the Common App. They have no records of their own here yet.

ApplyTexas, the Cal State Apply system and the SUNY application are further shared applications in this Destination. None of the fourteen institutions in this profile uses one, so none has been researched.

systems.name: The University of California application

jurisdiction.authority: Regents of the University of California
jurisdiction.area: The nine undergraduate campuses of the University of California

coverage.includes: All nine undergraduate University of California campuses — Berkeley, Davis, Irvine, Los Angeles, Merced, Riverside, San Diego, Santa Barbara and Santa Cruz — on one form, with campuses selected inside it.
coverage.excludes: Everything else in California. The California State University system has its own separate application, and the state's private universities are on the Common App or their own. The word "California" covers three unrelated application systems and this is only one of them.

choiceRules.note: One application, as many of the nine campuses as you like, 80 USD each and 95 USD each for an international applicant. Campuses are not ranked and each decides separately, so it is possible to be admitted by several and refused by others on the same file.

systems.identityRequirement: A UC application account. No US identity document is needed to apply.

fee.note: Per campus, for international and non-immigrant applicants. 80 USD per campus for domestic applicants.

sharedSteps: Open the application from 1 August and file it between 1 and 30 November. Nothing is accepted before or after that window.
Self-report the full academic record inside the application. UC reads what you enter; transcripts follow only if you enrol.
Answer four of the eight personal insight questions, 350 words each. There is no single long essay.
Do not collect teacher references. UC states that it does not require or read letters of recommendation at the time of application.
If you enrol, get the final transcript to the campus by 1 July and the official IB results by 15 July.
systems.decisionModel: Comprehensive review at each campus against its own priorities, with no early round of any kind and no rolling consideration. Decisions are released across March.
systems.replyModel: Admitted first-year students accept by submitting a Statement of Intent to Register (SIR) by 1 May. A SIR is to one campus only.

sources.title: For fall 2027 entry the University of California application opens on 1 August 2026, must be filed between 1 October and 30 November 2026, decisions are released during March 2027, admitted first-year students must submit their Statement of Intent to Register by 1 May 2027, and official IB examination results must reach the campus by 15 July 2027.

The University of California charges 80 USD per campus, 95 USD per campus for international and non-immigrant applicants, and does not require or read letters of recommendation at the time of application.

notes: Whether a non-resident applicant must satisfy any additional documentary step inside the application is not established here.

additionalGuidance.title: More about studying here
additionalGuidance.text: An American bachelor's degree takes four years and starts broad: you take courses across several fields and usually declare a major at the end of year two. Almost everything else about applying is set by the institution rather than by the country. There is no ministry of education that decides who qualifies, no national recognition body that converts an IB Diploma into anything, no minimum points, and no single deadline — the University of California closes on 30 November 2026 for a degree starting in autumn 2027, Harvard's regular round closes on 1 January 2027, Yale's on 2 January and MIT's on 4 January, and MIT is not on the same application form as any of them. What decides how you apply here is which application system your institution uses and what kind of institution it is. It is not which state it is in.
